claims.text: Ask directly whether the patient intends to hurt someone; asking does not make acting out more likely.
claims.quote: Speaking directly—mentioning that patients seem angry or upset, asking them if they intend to hurt someone—acknowledges their feelings and may elicit information; it does not make them more likely to act out.

claims.text: Take verbal threats seriously; in many places the clinician must warn the intended victim and notify law enforcement.
claims.quote: Verbal threats must be taken seriously. In many localities, when a patient expresses the intention to harm a particular person, the evaluating clinician is required to warn the intended victim and to notify law enforcement.
claims.locator: General Principles, Staff and public safety

claims.text: Collateral history from family, friends, caseworkers and medical records.
claims.quote: Because patients are often unable or unwilling to provide a clear history, other collateral sources of information (eg, family members, friends, caseworkers, medical records) must be identified and consulted immediately.

claims.text: Past violence is a strong predictor of future episodes.
claims.quote: A prior history of violence or aggression is a strong predictor of future episodes.

claims.text: Expressing homicidal intent counts as danger to others when deciding on involuntary hospitalization.
claims.quote: Danger to others includes Expressing homicidal intent

claims.text: Medical workup for new-onset or qualitatively different symptoms.
claims.quote: Assessment by history, physical examination, and sometimes laboratory testing or brain imaging (1) is required for patients with New-onset psychiatric symptoms (ie, no prior history of similar symptoms) Qualitatively different or unexpected symptoms in a patient with a known or stable psychiatric disorder

claims.text: Toxicology screen (urine drug screen, blood alcohol) with recent substance use or signs of it.
claims.quote: Toxicology screening (eg, urine drug screen, blood alcohol level) is done if the patient has a recent history of substance use disorder or physical signs suggesting intoxication or recent substance use (eg, needle marks).
